content.title: About
content.content: Tomato sauce for vegetables is a ready‑made sauce made from ripe tomatoes, aromatic herbs and spices, designed to dress and cook a variety of vegetable dishes. It has a rich tomato flavor, mild sweetness and a hint of acidity, making it a versatile addition to salads, casseroles, stews and grilled vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes used in the sauce are often greenhouse‑grown to ensure a consistent taste year‑round.
Traditional Italian tomato sauce recipes include basil, oregano and garlic, giving it a characteristic aroma.
Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene – a powerful antioxidant that gives tomatoes their bright red color.
In some countries the sauce is served cold as a dip for fresh vegetable sticks.
Heat‑processed tomatoes in sauce become more digestible, and their nutrients more bioavailable.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties, supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and beta‑carotene
items.content: Support vision, skin health and immunity.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Tomato sauce is typically low in calories, making it a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Helps regulate digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some ready‑made sauces can be high in salt; people with hypertension should opt for low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Sugar is sometimes added to improve taste, which may be undesirable for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: The sauce may contain garlic, onion or herbs that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain commercial sauces contain preservatives; choose additive‑free options if preferred.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the sauce to dress salads, as a base for vegetable casseroles, stews, grilled vegetables, or as a dip for fresh veggie sticks. It can also be warmed in a pan with a splash of olive oil to deepen the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in the refrigerator after opening in a tightly sealed jar. Once opened, it typically lasts 5‑7 days. Avoid contaminating the sauce with dirty utensils to prevent spoilage.
